feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications strategy and credible progression within one organization. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven communications.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Strong writing quality overall: concise, professional, and largely error-free, with good use of specific platforms and responsibilities.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include metrics tied to growth, engagement, efficiency, cost savings, campaign performance, or team impact.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would sharpen structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); and make punctuation/bullet formatting consistent, especially the dash-led bullets embedded in paragraphs.  

No major misspellings found. Minor style issue: “Coleman DAVIS” is visually inconsistent unless intentional for branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around senior leadership, public-sector relevance, and measurable scope will increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with sharper themes like cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and editorial systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, analytics, and communications operations across content, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear public-facing messaging and aligning stakeholders around effective digital strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/operational strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize consistently: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic and leadership-level capabilities over task-level items like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Consider: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web & CMS leadership • Editorial systems & governance • Multi-channel communications • Analytics, insights & reporting • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If space allows, replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with the more accessible “Workflow automation & systems design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates the header and Soft Skills section.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while technical tools remain in “Technical + IT.”

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance improvements to streamline organization-wide communications.”
- Consolidate web build details into one bullet: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable toolkits for member engagement.”
- Add measurable scope/results where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, or campaign performance improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” and “enterprise web improvement” repeat the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting impact instead.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; avoid repeating feature lists verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a multi-channel public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more strategic and measurable: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with results such as audience growth, engagement, send volume, or campaign impact if available.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current email/newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the 2018–2022 role.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears in the consultant role; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scale so it shows how this role set up the later director-level impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale/outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-based: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution: “Built editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version more tactical.
- Weekly advocacy video also appears in the 2015–2018 role and footer project list; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder-focused public-sector communications” if you want a more senior, less copywriter-style tone.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: “Enterprise web modernization strategy” or “Content governance for high-volume publishing.”
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid mixed forms like “messaging” vs. “planning” vs. “leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than experience-based strengths already shown in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat software lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not inventory-led: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is still central to current work.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths tied to recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, automation.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Platform integrations and publishing workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place unless this section is shortened.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI) • User behavior insights (Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive reporting • SEO and performance optimization”
- Group tools in parentheses to reduce list fatigue and improve scanability.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Board/executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, add one impact-oriented phrase tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization” or “decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless framed as optimization.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with more senior, delivery-oriented language: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera systems.”
- Reorder by impact/recency: put livestream/hybrid events and studio operations before basic editing.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “- Livestream and hybrid event production - Broadcast studio operations and buildout - PTZ and multi-camera video systems - Video production, editing and distribution”
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale signals in experience bullets rather than here (e.g., number of events, recurring series, in-house studio launched).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording here.
- “Video production and editing” is partly reinforced by Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro,” “Livestream studio workflows”), so this section should stay concise and strategic.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or differentiated with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant platforms first and de-emphasize lower-signal tools: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Consider adding proficiency/context instead of a flat list: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”
- Remove “GitHub Pages” unless it supports a meaningful project or portfolio outcome; it reads lighter than the rest.
- If space allows, align to recent impact: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [2]; keep one as a simple platform list and use the other for broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear elsewhere, so don’t repeat them here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support your recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)**
- Standardize phrasing: drop version numbers unless they matter; use parallel nouns/phrases (“API and tag implementation” vs mixed nouns/tools).
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end troubleshooting for Drupal sites**, **serverless scripting**, or **deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” are also referenced elsewhere, so keep this item tool-focused rather than repeating broad capability claims.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize systems ownership, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**.
- Tighten to the most relevant, differentiated tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**.
- Drop lower-value/general items unless central to recent work: **Basecamp** and **Trello** feel dated and less aligned with senior-level positioning.
- If format allows, add a short qualifier instead of a pure list: **Built and managed workflow systems using Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery through Jira, Asana, Slack and Microsoft Teams.**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not automation systems, so consider separating them if you want cleaner categorization.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform depth or campaign/automation capability rather than just listing tools.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add capability framing instead of a plain list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys (segmentation, journeys, campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp**
- Only keep all three if you’ve used each meaningfully; otherwise prioritize the most recent/relevant platforms tied to current and 2022–2024 work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating “email strategy/operations” here unless you add platform-specific depth.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate Higher Logic/community or analytics themes elsewhere unless clarified.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “firsts” or foundational contributions from this earlier period.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or video episodes produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with actions and results.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production support.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats themes covered more strongly in later leadership roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate project work into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the second sentence to one concrete achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scale or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders/program teams served, or audience/reach.
- Keep language modest and foundational so it supports career progression into later digital leadership roles rather than sounding duplicative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later entries on video, livestreams, and digital operations; keep this broader and less detailed.
- Avoid repeating “weekly video updates” or in-house digital team themes already covered in 2015–2024 roles.
